# cstar

> A C-family language (C#-like syntax, no garbage collector / RAII, explicit named parameters) that
> transpiles to portable C — running natively everywhere and in the browser via WebAssembly, with no
> runtime. Goal: a portable, lightweight WebGPU game engine. MIT licensed.

cstar's grammar is the source of truth (the compiler is a Flex lexer + Bison grammar + AST → C emitter).
Docs are generated from or point at that source so they never drift. For the authoritative syntax, read
the grammar; for semantics, read the spec; for runnable examples, read the test fixtures.

## Language
- [Specification (semantics overview)](docs/SPEC.md): types, named params, RAII, classes, inheritance, build/debug.
- [Grammar (BNF)](docs/grammar.bnf): authoritative syntax, generated from `cstar.y` by `tools/gen-grammar`.
- [Keyword status](docs/KEYWORDS.md): per-keyword audit (implemented / reserved / planned).
- [Goals & design philosophy](GOALS.md): no-GC, one-way/simplicity, explicit>implicit, self-describing, LLM-discoverable.

## Examples
- [tests/](tests/): each `*.cstar` is a runnable program with a `.expect` exit code. See
  `class_basic.cstar` (classes), `dtor_block.cstar` (RAII), `named_args.cstar` (named params),
  `refparam.cstar` (ref/out), and the inheritance/virtual fixtures.

## Toolchain & runtime
- [README](README.md): build/run via the containerized toolchain (`tools/cdev`); native + wasm targets;
  `cstar build [--release] [--target native|wasm]`.
- [Runtime header](cstar_runtime.h): the small C runtime included by generated code (`cstar_string`, trace hook).
- [Repo guide for AI assistants](CLAUDE.md): working conventions and build commands.

## Status
Implemented: functions, primitives, control flow, named-parameter calls, ref/out, classes, RAII
destructors, single inheritance + virtual dispatch, interfaces, enums; **generic collections**
(`Array<T>`/`List<T>`/`String`, monomorphized + RAII, `foreach`, bounds-checked `[]`); the full
**smart-pointer family** (`Owned<T>` unique, `Shared<T>` ref-counted, `Weak<T>` non-owning, with
move/retain semantics, auto-deref, RAII); **multi-file builds with private-by-default namespaces**
(`namespace X;` + `using`/aliases/qualified access; no-namespace files are file-private; shared header +
per-module .c); native + WASM + debug/release builds; IDE breakpoint debugging (VSCode extension in
`editor/vscode/`); **C FFI** (`extern` functions + `extern class` external structs, `extern "<header>"`
includes, opaque `Ptr`/`Ptr<T>` = void*/T*, `usize`, `addr(of:)` out-params, `string.cstr()`, `--link
<lib>`); raw pointer memory access is confined to an explicit **`unsafe { }`** block (M17 — the language's
entire unsafe surface, greppable), with a safe `dataPtr()`/`byteLen()` collection→buffer bridge. An
unlowered construct is a hard build error. **Function-pointer callbacks** (M18): `funcptr(of: freeFn)`
hands a cstar function to a C API as a function pointer (the callback type comes from the header; the
cstar signature must match its ABI) — controlled, no `unsafe`. When the C type isn't exactly spellable in
cstar (e.g. a `const` pointer), cast to the header's callback typedef: `cast<Cb>(funcptr(of: fn))` —
explicit, general (real libc `qsort` works this way). Planned (see `docs/ENGINE_READINESS.md`):
math types + operator overloading, `Map<K,V>` + general generics, tagged unions + match, an attribute
system + reflection (for declarative serialization), file I/O + networking; then cstar-level WebGPU
bindings.
